title.en: Whither Thou Goest: Ruth Gleans in Boaz's Field
title.zh: 你往哪裡去我也去：路得在波阿斯田拾穗

texts.period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Famine drives Elimelech's family to Moab; the men die, and Naomi returns home orphaned, telling her daughters-in-law to go back. Ruth's answer is one of the most quoted loyalties in literature: 'Whither thou goest, I will go... thy God my God'. In Bethlehem's barley harvest she gleans in the field of Boaz, who commands the harvesters to leave handfuls on purpose for 'the Moabite damsel'.
summary.zh: 饑荒驅以利米勒家往摩押；男丁盡亡，拿俄米喪夫喪子而歸，勸二媳回娘家。路得之答為文學中著名忠誠：「你往哪裡去，我也往那裡去……你的神就是我的神。」伯利恆割大麥時，她在波阿斯的田裡拾穗；波阿斯吩咐僕人「為那摩押女子留下」一把一把的麥穗。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ruth is read at Shavuot; her loyalty (chesed) frames the book's theology.

passages.text: And Ruth said: 'Entreat me not to leave thee, and to return from following after thee; for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God; where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried; the LORD do so to me, and more also, if aught but death part thee and me.'

Boaz told her to keep close to his maidens and drink of the water the young men had drawn: 'The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to take refuge'. At meal he handed her parched corn, and she 'did eat, and was sufficed, and left thereof'. Naomi read the field's owner as the family's redeemer — a near kinsman. Paraphrase of Ruth 2:8-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Spread Thy Skirt Over Thy Handmaid: The Threshing Floor
title.zh: 求你用你的衣襟遮蓋僕人：禾場之夜

texts.period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Naomi sends Ruth, washed and anointed, to the threshing floor by night to 'uncover his feet' and lie down. Waking at midnight, Boaz trembles — 'who art thou?' — 'I am Ruth thine handmaid... for thou art a near kinsman'. He blesses her kindness 'more than at the beginning', names the nearer kinsman obstacle, and loads her with six measures of barley before dawn.
summary.zh: 拿俄米遣沐浴抹膏的路得夜至禾場，「掀開他腳上的被」，躺臥其旁。半夜波阿斯驚起——「你是誰？」——「我是你的婢女路得……因為你是至近的親屬」。他祝福她的恩慈「比先前更大」，指出更近的親屬為難處，天亮前給她六簸箕大麥。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. 'Spread thy skirt' is proposal-language of protection/levirate rights.

passages.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was startled, and turned over; and, behold, a woman lay at his feet. And he said: 'Who art thou?' And she answered: 'I am Ruth thine handmaid; spread therefore thy skirt over thy handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.' And he said: 'Blessed be thou of the LORD, my daughter; for thou hast shown more kindness in the end than at the beginning.'

title.en: Sandals at the Gate: The Kinsman Redeemer
title.zh: 城門口脫鞋：至近的親屬

texts.period: Narrative set in the era of the Judges; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Boaz convenes ten elders at the gate; the nearer kinsman renounces Elimelech's field when it carries Ruth with it — the shoe drawn and given as witness. 'So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.' Obed is born, and the women bless Naomi: 'The LORD hath not left thee this day without a redeemer' — and the book closes with the genealogy that runs to David.
summary.zh: 波阿斯在城門口召十位長老；更近的親屬因田帶著路得而放棄——脫鞋為證。「波阿斯娶了路得為妻」。俄備得出生，婦女們祝福拿俄米：「耶和華是應當稱頌的，因為今日沒有撇下你無至近的親屬」——書末譜系直達大衛。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Levirate-marriage and sandal exchange are legal custom etiologies.

passages.text: And this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man drew off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour; and this was the manner of attestation in Israel. So the near kinsman said unto Boaz: 'Buy it for thee'; and he drew off his shoe.

title.en: Hadassah Who Hid Her Name: Esther Made Queen
title.zh: 隱名的哈大沙：以斯帖封后

texts.period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE (Ahasuerus/Xerxes era); composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Ahasuerus's hundred-and-eighty-day banquet ends with Queen Vashti refusing to parade her beauty and losing her throne. Orphaned Hadassah, 'and her Hebrew name was Esther', is gathered into the harem of the citadel at Shushan under Mordecai's watch; she tells 'not her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her'. The king loves her above all the women, 'and he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen'. Mordecai overhears an assassination plot and is recorded in the chronicles.
summary.zh: 亞哈隨魯一百八十日大宴，王后瓦實提拒絕展示美貌而失位。孤兒哈大沙——希伯來名以斯帖——在末底改囑咐下入書珊城宮，'不將籍贯宗族告訴人'。王愛她過於眾女，「把王后的冠冕戴在她頭上，立她為王后」。末底改偷聽弒君陰謀，事跡記於王上記錄。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim narrative origin; read with noise-making (graggers) at the Megillah.

passages.text: And the king loved Esther more than all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.

Esther was orphaned, 'the daughter of his father's brother', and 'Mordecai took her for his own daughter'. 'Esther had not made known her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not make it known.' In the king's gate Mordecai sat daily to learn her welfare — the careful concealment that makes the rescue to come possible. Paraphrase of Esther 2:5-11 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Haman's Lot and the Genocide Decree

texts.period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Mordecai will not bow to Haman the Agagite; fury builds until Haman casts lots (pur) for the day — the thirteenth of Adar — and wins the king's ring to write the decree of destruction for 'a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples... whose laws are diverse from every people'. Mordecai's message to Esther ends: 'who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' Esther fasts three days and enters unbidden: 'if I perish, I perish.'
summary.zh: 末底改不跪哈曼；怒氣積至哈曼掣普珥籤定十二月十三日，取得王戒寫滅族詔——針對「散居各國的那一民，他們的律例與萬民不同」。末底改寄語以斯帖：「焉知你得了王位，不是為現今的機會麼？」以斯帖禁食三日，未召擅入：「我若死就死吧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim's fast of Esther and the reading cycle recall this decree.

passages.text: And Mordecai told him to tell Esther: 'Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews. For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then will relief and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place, but thou and thy father's house will perish; and who knoweth whether thou art not come to the kingdom for such a time as this?'

'Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me... I also and my maidens will fast in like manner; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law; and if I perish, I perish.' For three days the city's Jews fasted 'with fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes'. Paraphrase of Esther 4:15-17; 3:8-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Banquets of Wine and the Gallows of Fifty Cubits

texts.period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Esther invites the king and Haman to a wine-banquet, then to a second; between the two, sleepless Ahasuerus is read the chronicles and learns Mordecai was never rewarded. The king asks Haman: 'What shall be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour?' — and Haman, certain it is himself, prescribes the royal horse and robe, then wears the humiliation home. At the second banquet Esther names the plot, and Haman is hanged on the very gallows he built for Mordecai.
summary.zh: 以斯帖兩次設酒宴請王與哈曼；其間失眠的亞哈隨魯聞記錄而得知末底改未受報賞。王問哈曼：「王所喜悅尊榮的人，當將他如何待呢？」——哈曼自以為是，獻上王服御馬之禮，回家蒙羞。二次宴上以斯帖道破陰謀；哈曼被掛在他為末底改所預備的木架上。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Haman answered the king: 'For the man whom the king delighteth to honour, let the royal apparel be brought which the king useth to wear, and the horse that the king rideth upon... and let the apparel and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king's most noble princes, that they may array the man withal whom the king delighteth to honour, and cause him to ride on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaim before him: Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delighteth to honour.'

At the second banquet Esther unveiled: 'we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed... for we are sold into death'. The king left the chamber in fury; Haman fell on the queen's couch pleading — and the king returned to the accusation, 'Will he even force the queen before me in the house?' Harbonah mentioned the fifty-cubit gallows at Haman's house; 'hang him thereon' — 'so they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai; then was the king's wrath pacified.' Paraphrase of Esther 7:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

texts.period: Narrative set c. 5th-4th c. BCE; composed c. 4th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Esther's counter-decree lets the Jews defend themselves; Mordecai in royal apparel goes out from the king's presence, 'and the city of Shushan shouted and was glad'. The fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar are fixed by letters 'sent among all the Jews... as days of feasting and joy, and sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor' — Purim instituted, and the book's own name ('these words, the Purim') canonized in the story's last verses.
summary.zh: 以斯帖的對等詔書准猶太人自衛；末底改穿朝服出王門，「書珊城的人民都歡呼快樂」。亞達月十四、十五日由書信定為「設筵歡樂、彼此饋送禮物、賙濟窮人」之日——普珥節設立，書末經文自身（「這就是普珥節」）被收錄於故事之中。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Purim is a living festival; the record describes the institution narrative.

passages.text: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and which had come unto them, the Jews established, and took upon them, and upon their seed, and upon all such as joined themselves unto them, so that it should not fail, that they would keep these two days according to the writing thereof, and according to the appointed time thereof, every year.

texts.period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE (exilic era); composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Exiled youths of Judah's royal seed are renamed for Babylon's gods; Daniel resolves 'that he would not defile himself with the king's dainties'. His test of ten days' pulse and water ends with faces 'fairer, and fatter in flesh' than all who ate the king's food — 'and God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom'.
summary.zh: 猶大王室被擄少年被改名歸巴比倫諸神；但以理立志「不以王的膳和王所飲的酒玷污自己」。十日素菜白水的試驗，他們的面貌「比用王膳的一切少年人更加俊美肥胖」——「神在各樣文字學問上賜給他們聰明知識」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer, and they were fatter in flesh, than all the youths that did eat of the king's dainties. ... And as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 1:15, 17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The Great Image of Nebuchadnezzar's Dream

texts.period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Nebuchadnezzar demands that his wise men reveal both dream and interpretation; all fail and the decree of death goes out. Daniel prays with his friends and receives the secret 'in a vision of the night'. Before the king he recounts the great image — head of gold, breast of silver, belly of brass, legs of iron, feet of iron and clay — smitten by a stone 'cut out without hands' that fills the whole earth: 'there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.'
summary.zh: 尼布甲尼撒命哲士顯明夢與講解；皆不能，殺令已出。但以理與同伴祈禱，夜間異象中得奧秘。他在王前述大像——金頭、銀胸、銅腹、鐵腿、半鐵半泥的腳——被「非人手鑿出來的石頭」擊碎，那石頭變成充滿天下的大山：「天上的神能顯明奧秘的事。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Four-kingdoms schema foundational to Jewish and Christian apocalyptic.

passages.text: Thou, O king, sawest, and, behold, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was surpassing, stood before thee; and the look thereof was terrible. As for that image, the head thereof was of fine gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass, its legs of iron, its feet part of iron and part of clay.

'Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon its feet... and the gold, the silver, the brass, the iron, the clay... became like the chaff of the summer threshing-floors; and the wind carried them away... and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.' Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face and exalted Daniel, setting him over the province of Babylon. Paraphrase of Daniel 2:34-49 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Fourth Man in the Fire

texts.period: Narrative set c. 6th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: All nations must bow at the music to the golden image on the plain of Dura. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego answer: 'our God... is able to deliver us... but if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods'. Cast bound into the furnace heated sevenfold, they walk unbound in the flames — and the king sees 'a fourth man... like to a son of the gods' walking with them. The fire has 'no smell of fire' upon their clothes.
summary.zh: 樂聲一起，各族都當拜杜拉平原的金像。沙得拉、米煞、亞伯尼歌答：「我們的神能救我們……即或不然，王啊，你當知道我們決不事奉你的神。」被捆著扔進七倍的火窰，他們在火中自由行走——王見「第四個……好像神子」與他們同行。他們衣服上火燎的氣味也沒有。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste, and spoke, and said unto his counsellors: 'Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?' They answered and said unto the king: 'True, O king.' He answered and said: 'But I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'

title.en: Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin: The Hand on the Wall
title.zh: 彌尼彌尼提客勒烏法珥新：牆上的手

region.en: Great hall of Belshazzar's feast, Babylon
region.zh: 伯沙撒宴會大廳，巴比倫

texts.period: Narrative set 539 BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Belshazzar toasts his gods from the vessels of the Jerusalem Temple — 'and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone' — when fingers come forth and write on the plaster. None can read it; the queen mother remembers Daniel. The judgment: 'MENE, God hath numbered thy kingdom... TEKEL, thou art weighed in the balances... PERES, thy kingdom is divided'. That night Belshazzar is slain and Darius the Mede takes the kingdom.
summary.zh: 伯沙撒用耶路撒冷聖殿的器皿飲酒，「讚美金銀銅鐵木石所造的神」——手指顯現於粉牆寫字。無人能讀；太后想起但以理。審判：「彌尼，就是神已經數算你國的年日……提客勒，就是被秤在天平裡顯出你的虧欠……毘勒斯，就是你的國分裂」。當夜伯沙撒被殺，瑪代人大流士取國。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaster of the wall of the king's palace; and the king saw the palm of the hand that wrote. Then the king's countenance was changed in him, and his thoughts affrighted him; and the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another.

texts.period: Narrative set c. 6th-5th c. BCE; composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Envious presidents frame an irrevocable law: prayer to any god or man but the king for thirty days is lion-food. Daniel, knowing it, opens his windows toward Jerusalem and prays three times a day 'as he did aforetime'. Cast into the den, he is sealed in overnight; at dawn the king cries: 'O Daniel, servant of the living God... is thy God able to deliver thee?' — 'My God hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.' The accusers go in instead, and Darius decrees the God of Daniel 'the living God, and stedfast for ever'.
summary.zh: 嫉妒的總長設立不可更改之令：三十日內凡向王以外的神或人祈禱者，必扔獅坑。但以理知道這禁令，仍面向耶路撒冷開窗，一日三次禱告「與素常一樣」。被扔坑中，封石過夜；黎明王呼：「活神的僕人但以理啊……你的神能救你脫離獅子麼？」——「我的神差遣使者，封住獅子的口。」控告者反倒被扔進去；大流士降旨宣認「活神，永遠長存」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then said Daniel unto the king: 'O king, live for ever. My God hath sent His angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me; forasmuch as before Him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.' ... So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he had trusted in his God.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Daniel 6:21-23 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Four Beasts and the Ancient of Days

region.en: Heavenly court (vision; symbolic pin at Babylon)
region.zh: 天庭（異象；以巴比倫象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 6th-2nd c. BCE (vision dated to first year of Belshazzar); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Four great beasts rise from the churning sea — lion with eagle's wings, bear, leopard with four wings, and a terrifying fourth with iron teeth and ten horns. 'The Ancient of Days did sit, whose raiment was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool': judgment sits, the books are opened, the fourth beast burns. 'I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like a son of man came with the clouds of heaven... and there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom.'
summary.zh: 四巨獸自攪動的海中上來——鷹翼獅、熊、四翼豹、十角鐵齒的可怕第四獸。「亙古常在者坐著，衣服潔白如雪，頭髮如純淨的羊毛」：審判設立，案卷展開，第四獸焚燒。「我在夜間的異象中觀看，見有一位像人子的，駕著天雲而來……得了權柄、榮耀、國度。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The four-kingdoms vision anchors apocalyptic eschatology in Jewish and Christian tradition.

passages.text: I beheld till thrones were placed, and One that was Ancient of Days did sit; His raiment was as white snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool; His throne was fiery flames, and the wheels thereof burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before Him; thousand thousands ministered unto Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him; the judgment was set, and the books were opened.

The son-of-man figure receives 'dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion... which shall not be destroyed'. The vision's angel-interpreter explains the beasts as kings and kingdoms, with the saints of the Most High inheriting at the end. Paraphrase of Daniel 7:13-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jonah Flees, the Sea Rages, and the Fish Waits
title.zh: 約拿逃避，海翻騰，大魚等候

region.zh: 約帕外的地中海（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Ordered to cry against Nineveh, Jonah rises to flee to Tarshish — 'from the presence of the LORD'. A great wind; the mariners cast lots and find the Hebrew passenger, asleep below: 'What meanest thou, O thou sleeper?' Thrown overboard at his own insistence, 'and the sea ceased from her raging' — and 'the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.' From the deep he prays; the fish vomits him on dry land.
summary.zh: 受命往尼尼微呼喊，約拿卻起身逃往他施——「躲避耶和華」。大風驟起；水手掣籤尋出這希伯來乘客，他在船底沉睡：「你這沉睡的人哪，這是怎樣呢？」依他自己的話被拋入海，海便平靜——「耶和華安排一條大魚吞了約拿；他在魚腹中三日三夜」。他在深處禱告；魚把他吐在旱地上。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Jonah read complete on Yom Kippur afternoon; the fish-belly prayer is penitential.

passages.text: And he said unto them: 'Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you; for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.' ... So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea; and the sea ceased from her raging. ... And the LORD prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Jonah 1:12, 15, 17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: From the belly he prayed: 'I called by reason of mine affliction, unto the LORD... The waters compassed me about, even to the soul; the deep was round about me... yet hast Thou brought up my life from the pit, O LORD my God.' 'And the LORD spoke unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.' Paraphrase of Jonah 2:1-10 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Repentance of Nineveh and the Gourd

region.en: Nineveh, great city on the Tigris
region.zh: 尼尼微，底格里斯河大城

texts.period: Composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The second commission succeeds absurdly: one day's preaching and 'the men of Nineveh believed God... from the greatest of them even to the least of them' — even the cattle fast in sackcloth. God relents, and Jonah sulks: 'it displeased Jonah exceedingly'. Under his booth God grows a gourd for shade, then smites it with a worm; Jonah's pity for the plant draws the book's closing question: 'Should not I have pity on Nineveh, that great city... and also much cattle?'
summary.zh: 第二次使命荒謬地成功：一天的呼喊，尼尼微人「信服神……從最大的到至小的」——連牲畜都披麻禁食。神後悔不滅，約拿發怒大大不悅。棚下神使蓖麻生長遮蔭，又以蟲咬之枯；約拿為樹惜命，書末神問：「這尼尼微大城……我豈能不愛惜呢？何況其中……並許多牲畜呢？」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city. And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head. ... And God said to Jonah: 'Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd?' ... Then said the LORD: 'Thou hast had pity on the gourd... and should not I have pity on Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons... and also much cattle?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Jonah 4:5-11 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The Wager in Heaven: Job Loses Everything
title.zh: 天上的賭局：約伯盡失所有

region.en: Land of Uz (location unknown; symbolic pin)
region.zh: 烏斯地（地點不詳；象徵性定位）

texts.period: Frame narrative composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; poetic core c. 5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: 'There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was whole-hearted and righteous'. In the heavenly council 'the satan' — the adversary — challenges his piety as bought: 'Doth Job fear God for nought?' Permission given, four messengers take children, oxen, sheep, and camels — 'and I only am escaped alone to tell thee'. Job rends his mantle: 'The LORD hath given, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.' Struck with boils, he still does not sin 'with his lips' — but the arguments that follow are the longest in the Bible.
summary.zh: 「烏斯地有一個人名叫約伯；那人完全正直，敬畏神，遠離惡事」。天庭會議中，「那撒但」——控告者——指其虔誠為有價：「約伯敬畏神，豈是無故呢？」許可之下，四個報信者相繼而至——兒女牛羊駱駝盡失——「惟有我一人逃脫，來報信給你」。約伯撕裂外袍：「賞賜的是耶和華，收取的也是耶和華；耶和華的名是應當稱頌的。」長瘡而不「以口犯罪」——但其後的辯論是聖經中最長的。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The satan is a member of the divine council in the frame, not the later devil.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto the satan: 'Hast thou set thy heart on My servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a whole-hearted and an upright man, one that feareth God, and shunneth evil.' Then the satan answered: 'Doth Job fear God for nought? Hast not Thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?... But put forth Thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce Thee to Thy face.'

In one day came the Sabeans, fire of God, Chaldeans, and the great wind; 'there came another, and said: Thy sons and thy daughters were eating... and, behold, there came a great wind... and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee'. In the whirlwind-dialogues Job demands a hearing from God; the speeches from the storm answer with snow-critters and crocodiles — 'Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?' — and Job's answer closes the matter: 'I have heard of Thee by the hearing of the ear; but now mine eye seeth Thee; wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.' Paraphrase of Job 1:13-19; 38-42 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The LORD Turned the Captivity of Job
title.zh: 耶和華使約伯從苦境轉回

texts.period: Frame narrative composed c. 6th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The frame resumes: the LORD rebukes the friends — 'My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken of Me the thing that is right, as hath My servant Job' — and requires a sacrifice with Job as intercessor. 'And the LORD turned the captivity of Job... and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.' Seven sons and three daughters again; the daughters are named, Jemima, Kezia, and Keren-happuch, 'and there were not found such fair women as the daughters of Job'.
summary.zh: 敘事框架重啟：耶和華責備三友——「我的怒氣向你和你兩個朋友發作，因為你們議論我，不如我的僕人約伯說的是」——並要他們獻祭、由約伯代求。「耶和華就使約伯從苦境轉回……賜給他的比他從前所有的加倍」。又有七子三女；女兒得留名——耶米瑪、基洗亞、基連哈樸——「在那全地的婦女中，找不著像約伯的女兒那樣美貌的」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends; and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. ... And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. So Job died, being old and full of days.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Job 42:10, 15-17 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Ezra Reads the Law to the Weeping People
title.zh: 以斯拉誦律法於哭泣之民

texts.period: Narrative set c. 444 BCE; composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: At the water gate all Israel 'gather themselves together with one accord' to hear Ezra the scribe read the law of Moses from morning till midday; the Levites 'caused the people to understand the reading'. The people weep; the leaders' counter-command becomes liturgy: 'This day is holy unto the LORD... go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet... for the joy of the LORD is your strength.' They find written the festival of booths and keep it with branches as not done 'since the days of Jeshua'.
summary.zh: 在水門以色列眾人「如同一人」聚集，從清早到晌午聽文士以斯拉讀摩西的律法書；利未人「使百姓明白所念的」。百姓哭泣；首領的回令成為禮儀：「今日是耶和華你們神的聖日……你們去喫肥美的，喝甘甜的……因靠耶和華而得的喜樂是你們的力量。」他們尋得棚節之例，取枝搭棚，「從嫩的兒子約書亞的時候直到這日，以色列人沒有這樣行過」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Foundational for the synagogue Torah service.

passages.text: And they found written in the law, that the LORD had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month... So the people went forth, and brought them, and made them every one to sit upon the roof of his house, and in their courts... and in the broad places of the city. And there was very great gladness.

title.en: Nehemiah Builds the Wall in Fifty-Two Days
title.zh: 尼希米五十二日重建城牆

texts.period: Narrative set c. 445 BCE; composed c. 5th-4th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes, hears of the broken walls and prays four months; the king notes his sad face — 'why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste' — and grants leave and timber. Inspecting the ruins by night, he rallies the people, who build 'every one over against his own house' with tool in one hand and weapon in the other. Conspiracy letters cannot stop the work: 'the wall was finished... in fifty and two days'.
summary.zh: 波斯的王酒政尼希米聞城牆倒塌，禁食祈禱四月；王見其面帶愁容——「我列祖墳墓所在的那城荒涼，我豈能面無愁容麼」——賜准與木料。夜間騎牲口巡視廢墟，號召百姓「各對著自己的房屋修造」，一手作工一手拿兵器。仇敵書信未能止工：「城牆修完了……共修了五十二天。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they all of them sought to frighten us, thinking: 'They will let alone the work, that they be not done.' ... But I prayed, and set a watch against them day and night. And I said unto the nobles, and to the rulers and the rest of the people: 'The work is great and large, and we are separated upon the wall, one far from another; in what place thereof ye hear the sound of the horn, resort ye thither unto us; our God shall fight for us.'
